headline: High-risk workspace leakage and cascading errors: Notion AI can read shared workspace content while the prompt-list agent is unverified and may be copied into it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a prompt-writing/content source with no execution or isolation controls; B is a workspace Q&A agent that reads pages/databases and can ingest workspace text as context. That creates a plausible injection path if A’s prompts are pasted into Notion pages or queried through B. The pairwise bridge is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A-generated prompt text is copied into a Notion page that B reads
IF B is asked to summarize or act on workspace content containing attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Add a review step before pasting A output into Notion
Prefix imported prompt text as quoted/untrusted
Restrict B to specific pages for testing
Train users to ignore instructions inside retrieved content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for workspace content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has no network egress, so it is not a leak source. B can access workspace pages/databases and sends queries to vendor backends/downstream model providers, so sensitive workspace content can leave the workspace when B processes it. Because A is content-writing only, the pair risk is mainly that A-produced text may be mixed with workspace data and exposed through B.
conditions: IF A output is stored in a workspace page that contains sensitive material
IF B is invoked on pages or databases containing confidential content
mitigations: Limit B to non-sensitive pages
Move sensitive drafts out of shared workspace
Use a separate workspace for prompt libraries
Review retention settings for Notion AI
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels before AI access

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or network capabilities; B also cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and its mutable surface is limited to Notion workspace content. There is little direct write-write conflict between the pair. The only overlap is workspace content editing, which is not a filesystem or git collision and is lower blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are used to edit the same Notion page concurrently
IF users treat workspace pages as shared mutable state without review
mitigations: Assign one editor per page
Use page locks or edit windows
Separate prompt-library pages from operational notes
Review changes before publishing
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A agent grounded in workspace content, so it may treat A-produced text as authoritative if that text is placed in pages it reads. A itself only writes prompts/content, but B can summarize or act on that content without a built-in verification step. The pathway exists in default use, though the downstream action scope is limited to workspace outputs.
conditions: IF A output is inserted into a page that B uses as grounding
IF B is asked to answer questions or draft content from that page without human verification
mitigations: Mark A-generated text as untrusted
Require human review before publishing B outputs
Use source-linked prompts in Notion pages
Limit B to retrieval-only workflows
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gating before actioning outputs

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source content-writing with no touched data classes, while B handles workspace pages and team knowledge base content under vendor-hosted processing. That creates a compliance mismatch around retention and residency for workspace data, especially if sensitive internal content is placed into Notion AI. The other agent is not cited because A has no documented compliance surface beyond being a prompt repository.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain regulated or confidential data
IF Notion AI processing is enabled for those pages
mitigations: Exclude regulated pages from AI use
Review Notion retention and sharing settings
Separate public prompt libraries from internal knowledge bases
Document approved data classes for B
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated content
